title: a cut's step 8 reads each remote back once, within 15 s, and reports a read that did not answer as the remote not holding the release -- the 0.1.10 cut stopped with both remotes holding it, and a resume finished it
body:
FOUND 2026-10-08 in the 0.1.10 cut, and carried as vc's todo 153 until hv lifted the demo hold on 2026-10-14 and work recommenced. Filed without a scheduling question, under hv's batch-release directive.

WHAT HAPPENED. The cut (tmp/release/20261008-2021.RELEASE.out) passed its gates, tagged v0.1.10 at bb1cd07c, and pushed main and the tag to local and to upstream. Step 8 then stopped: "8 push FAILED upstream does not hold the release after the push: did not answer within 15s", followed by "Fix what the row names, then run again." Upstream did hold it. The resume three minutes later (tmp/release/20261008-2034.RELEASE.out) read "8 push already every remote holds the release commit on main and v0.1.10" and ended "v0.1.10 is released." CI's run on the tag, 37840059863, had started at 20:31:20Z.

WHAT THE CODE DOES, read by vc at main ca0d41a6, whose lib/ is 99dd3106's:
- After a remote's pushes, step 8 reads it back with `release_wait 0 "" UNREADABLE release_read_remote ...` (lib/cmd/release:913). A wait of 0 with no state to keep asks once, and the ask is bounded at the time left or RELEASE_ASK_FLOOR_SECONDS, whichever is larger (lib/release.steps:1070), so the floor's 15 s (lib/release.steps:1034) is the whole read-back. Steps 9 and 11 wait through the same function with a real wait and states to keep polling on (lib/cmd/release:947, :1059); step 8 does not.
- Any answer but `already` fails the step as "<remote> does not hold the release after the push: <detail>" (lib/cmd/release:914). An ask that runs out of time answers UNREADABLE (lib/release.steps:1074-1075), as does an ls-remote that fails (lib/release.steps:605), so a read that never came back is reported as the remote not holding the release. The row is false in exactly the case that happened, at the one point in a cut where the pushes cannot be taken back and the operator is told to fix what the row names.
- DEVBIN_RELEASE_ASK_FLOOR_SECONDS overrides the floor for the arms and is "not a project setting" (lib/release.steps:1019-1024), so the operator has no supported knob either.

THE ARM. releasecut.bats:2001 drives a remote that stops answering after the push and asserts step 8 FAILED with "did not answer within" inside 30 s. It holds today's behaviour, and no arm drives a remote that is slow once and then answers.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO (cc builds it and vc reviews it):
- Step 8 waits through UNREADABLE the way steps 9 and 11 wait through theirs: it asks again every RELEASE_POLL_SECONDS, up to a bound long enough for a remote that is slow straight after a push, and fails only when the last answer is still UNREADABLE. A `pending` or `refused` answer still fails at once. The builder chooses the bound and says why.
- The row says what was read. An UNREADABLE answer reads as could not read back whether <remote> holds the release, with its detail; "does not hold the release" stays for a remote that answered without it.
- Arms: releasecut.bats:2001 keeps its claim with the new bound and the new words, kept fast by an override for the arms as the floor's is. A remote that does not answer once and then holds the release passes step 8 and pushes nothing twice. A remote that accepts the push and does not keep the tag still fails step 8 at once (releasecut.bats:1646). Red first on main, green under BSD and GNU.
- Pages: lib/pages/release.md, where step 8 is described (:21-22).

It ships in the next release, with everything open.

## Resolution

Landed at 60b79891 on a green full suite (20261017-0636 (vc's landing suite at ca557b4d: 2384 of 2384 ok, 5 skips, .errors empty, 06:36:33Z to 06:45:14Z; seal kept in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-vc/clone-archive/seals/20261017-0636/)).

- **Step 8 waits through a read-back that got no answer.** After its pushes to a remote, step 8 reads it back and asks again every 15 s, up to the push's own bound (RELEASE_CALL_SECONDS, 120 s, so about 135 s with the last ask's floor), where it used to ask once within 15 s.
- **The row says what was read.** A read still unanswered at the bound fails as "could not read back whether <remote> holds the release after the push", with its detail, never as the remote not holding it. A remote that answered without the release fails at once, as before, and so does an answer that cannot be read here, such as a head this checkout does not hold, since the read-back never fetches.
- **Arms:** four in releasecut.bats. The hung read-back keeps its claim in the new words, and a remote slow once then answering passes with nothing pushed twice. A kept-tag failure and an unheld head each fail at once. 3 of the 4 are red first on main, the kept-tag arm green there by design, and all are green under BSD and GNU.
- **Page:** help release, step 8.

Declared:
- each remote waits on its own, so two unanswering remotes hold a cut about 135 s each;
- a wait that cannot make its scratch directory reads as a read-back that waited.
